newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stock investors protest at price decline.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stock investors protest at price decline.

text.p: Thousands of small investors, most of them operating in the unofficial kerb market, demonstrated outside the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) on Tuesday as share prices extended recent falls in early trade.

"We are smelling an avalanche in share prices, and such fears were boosted by a newspaper report on Monday that a government probe might expose those who manipulated the market," said investor Zahirul Islam.
He said any action against the alleged manipulators, who might include big market players, could plunge the DSE into a crisis of confidence.

The government in December appointed an inquiry committee, headed by Aminul Islam, professor of economics at Jahangirnagar University, to investigate an unusual rise in share prices during October-November and a nose-dive since then.
The committee is expected to submit its report to Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria in the next few days.
The DSE all share price index closed 86.52 points or 6.97 percent down at 1,153.52 on a turnover of 70.6 million taka on Monday. The index jumped to over 3,600 points in mid-November.
The Observer said on Monday in a report quoting a "competent source" that alleged market manipulators would lose their trading licences and may be jailed for five years.
